title: Corner & Cure deli storefront menu tiles: neutralise eight mixed-light dish captures to an in-frame grey card by eye, land one gritty-warm house look, license and grade a counter-paper backdrop, deepen a clashing red liner in-family, prep-and-vectorize the wordmark, cut the featured hero to transparency, and data-merge one storefront tile per dish

source.reference: Graphic designer needed: food-delivery storefront banner for a NY-style sandwich brand

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief (a scrappy NY-style sandwich shop needing storefront art for a food-delivery ordering app: 'gritty, bold, and a little chaotic - think New York deli meets Nonna's kitchen meets street culture, not polished or corporate'; 'we have the assets, they just need to be pulled together so they look like they were shot in the same image... one cohesive, intentional photo, not a collage'). Laundered to a fictional coined brand, 'Corner & Cure' (@cornerandcure) - no real company, person, product, or trademark named - and the real delivery marketplace is laundered to a generic 'food-delivery ordering-app storefront'. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the raw brief implied freehand Photoshop compositing of a single banner (drop layers onto a canvas by eye), which is NOT connector-doable (no from-scratch canvas layout, no generative fill, no move-tool compositing) - and the prior version of this task tried to bind the four photos into an Illustrator banner via document_merge_data_vector, which is TEXT-ONLY and can never carry an image column, so it would have printed empty frames. So the client is modeled as needing what the connectors genuinely produce: a per-DISH storefront menu-tile set (one hand-authored SINGLE-RECORD InDesign tile template, one file per row) plus a featured app-hero cutout. The Adobe chain does the real work the brief rewards: neutralise every dish photo to the in-frame grey card it carries so the whole set shares one white point and reads as one shoot, author one gritty-warm house look and hold it across differently-lit frames, license and grade a counter-paper backdrop from Adobe Stock, deepen a clashing bright-red liner to the house oxblood without a reshoot, prep-and-vectorize the wordmark, lift the featured hero onto transparency, then run the authored template through a one-file-per-row image+text data-merge and export a press-ready tile per dish. The single-cohesive-storefront intent and audience are preserved.
one_line_ask: Neutralise eight differently-lit deli dish photos to the grey card each one carries so the set reads as one shoot, decide per frame how far to move white balance and tone toward one gritty-warm house look without wrecking any dish's true colour, license and match-grade a counter-paper backdrop, deepen a clashing bright-red liner to the house oxblood in-family, prep and vectorize the wordmark, lift the featured hero onto transparency for the app hero slot, then data-merge the client's authored single-record tile template against the menu roster to produce one press-ready storefront tile per dish.
full_brief: Corner & Cure is a scrappy New-York-style sandwich shop - gritty, bold, a little chaotic, think NY deli meets Nonna's kitchen meets street culture, not polished or corporate. We are building out our food-delivery ordering-app storefront and need a clean menu tile for every dish, each carrying the dish name, item code, price and a short description, sitting on a rustic counter-paper texture with our wordmark crisp at the top - and the featured pastrami also lifted out for the big hero slot. We are NOT reshooting. We are handing you eight existing dish photos, and here is the problem: they were shot across a busy service under different light - some under cool fluorescents, some under warm tungsten, a couple under-/over-exposed, on different counters - so straight out of the folder they look like a mismatched jumble, and a storefront of mismatched shots reads cheap. To make this checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. Your job on the photos: bring every image to one consistent, true-to-dish look by neutralising each one to the grey card it contains - the card must read as a clean neutral grey (equal across the channels) in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set will share one white point. On top of that, give the set our house look: warm and golden, deep matte shadows that never crush to pure black, rich but not neon colour, so every dish reads like the same appetising shoot. But do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch - each photo was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target. Be careful: at least one dish is genuinely golden (the baked four-cheese mac is supposed to look deep and warm); if its grey card already reads neutral, do not 'cool' it chasing an imagined blue cast, or you will strip the colour we are selling. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure moves you made on each frame so we can confirm they are matched, not eyeballed. Next: source a rustic counter-paper / butcher-paper texture for the tile background and bring it into the same warm look so it doesn't clash. One of the pickle shots has a bright pillar-box red gingham liner that fights our brand - give us a version where that liner is deepened to our house oxblood-maroon (a rich, dark wine-red in the SAME colour family, just deepened and muted - not a jump to a far-off hue), and it has to sit under the real folds, weave and shadow of the liner, with the white checks left white and the pickles and counter untouched - no flat dead-fill, no whole-image tint. Our wordmark only exists as a flat sign lift on off-white paper - get it clean and razor-sharp so it never looks fuzzy at masthead size. Lift the featured pastrami cleanly so it can drop onto the counter-paper backdrop in the big hero slot without a hard rectangular photo edge - that hard edge is what makes it look like a collage. Finally, build the tiles: we have hand-built the InDesign tile template with the real placeholder fields and three image slots (background, dish photo, and the wordmark masthead), and we are giving you the menu roster; merge them so every dish gets its own single tile with its copy bound, its matching graded photo dropped in, the backdrop behind it and the crisp wordmark on top, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI PDF covering every dish (one tile per dish, the featured pastrami simply among them, page one). Bind the copy verbatim from the roster - do not rewrite our names or prices. Keep it gritty and warm; do not make it clean-corporate. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set matched to one white point; the backdrop matched to the look; the liner recolour natural under the existing light; the wordmark crisp vector; the hero cleanly on transparency; and exactly one finished tile per roster row.

inputs.name: corner_and_cure_tile_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD portrait storefront menu tile sized to the food-delivery app's item-tile spec (4x5in / 1200x1500px at 300 DPI) - ONE dish per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<dish_name>>, <<item_code>>, <<price>>, <<description>>, <<tagline>>, <<handle>>, and THREE @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate image frames: a full-bleed background frame bound to @Backdrop (the shared graded counter-paper texture), a dish-photo frame bound to @Dish (that row's graded photo), and a masthead frame bound to @Wordmark (the shared vectorized wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the backdrop, dish photo and wordmark each reach the tile ONLY as a merge bind through their image frame - none are dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and ALL THREE image frames actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW - so a single-record menu tile is the correct connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. The original spec's Illustrator/document_merge_data_vector path could never have worked (vector merge is TEXT-ONLY and cannot bind an image column) - this InDesign template with THREE image columns is the fix. @Backdrop and @Wordmark carry the SAME asset in every row so the shared texture and mark land on every tile as a merge bind, never free-form placement.

inputs.name: corner_and_cure_menu_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns dish_name,item_code,price,description,tagline,handle,@Dish,@Wordmark,@Backdrop holding EIGHT deli menu rows, one per dish: Hand-Cut Pastrami on Rye, Cured Italian Sub, House Dill Pickles, Slow-Drip Diner Coffee, Baked Four-Cheese Mac, Chopped Deli Salad, Loaded Chili Fries, Pastrami Hash Skillet. Each row carries a short appetite-driving one-to-two-line menu description, an item code (e.g. CC-SND-07), a US-dollar price (e.g. $14.50), the shared tagline 'STACKED HIGH. SERVED FAST.' and the shared handle '@cornerandcure'. The @Dish column names the matching prepped photo file (e.g. @pastrami_tile.jpg) so the [T] merge drops each graded photo into that row's tile; @Wordmark holds the SAME vectorized mark file (@corner_and_cure_wordmark.svg) in every row; @Backdrop holds the SAME graded texture file (@backdrop_graded.jpg) in every row. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields and the three @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Supplies the per-tile copy so the [T] merge binds it into the authored template; headers match the .indd fields and all three @image columns so binding works. Eight rows => the merge must produce EXACTLY eight finished tiles (page-count = row-count gate). @Wordmark and @Backdrop carry the identical file path in all eight rows, giving the chain-produced wordmark SVG and graded backdrop a connector-doable path onto every tile via the merge. Nothing in this roster encodes which capture is the trap or how any frame should be graded - the @Dish names are the agent's own post-triage outputs.

inputs.name: raw_deli_captures_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures of deli dishes, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera, roughly 4000x4000 or larger before crop), each with a photographic 18% grey reference card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral target. Shot across a busy service under deliberately mismatched light so straight out of the folder they look like a mismatched jumble: (1) a towering hand-cut pastrami-on-rye stacked high with steaming pink-cured meat and a toothpick, on a dark brushed-steel counter, cool bluish fluorescent cast, frame tilted ~4 deg; (2) a cured Italian sub cut in half on light butcher paper, harsh warm tungsten light, slightly overexposed on one side, frame tilted ~3 deg; (3) a metal basket of house dill pickle spears on a bright RED-and-white gingham deli liner, cool flat grey daylight, frame tilted ~4 deg; (4) a paper cup of black drip coffee with steam on a dark scratched diner counter, dim muddy warm light, underexposed, level; (5) a cast-iron of baked four-cheese mac that is GENUINELY deep golden-brown, shot under near-neutral light so its grey card already reads neutral (the warmth is the real food, not a white-balance error), level; (6) a chopped deli salad heavy with green romaine and herbs on light butcher paper, cool cast, level; (7) loaded chili fries under blown warm light, overexposed with clipped highlights on one edge, level; (8) a pastrami hash skillet under near-neutral light, frame tilted ~3 deg. Every shot has real crumb/grease/glaze/brine/fabric texture, cluttered deli-counter surroundings, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in each.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each tile crop fills the 1200x1500 tile frame at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY - no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set: cool-cast frames (1/3/6) must be WARMED, warm-cast frames (2/4/7) must be COOLED, and they sit on different counters (dark steel/diner counters 1/4 are low-key and need careful shadow lift; light butcher paper 2/6 is high-key) so one global black-point/exposure move breaks them too. Frame 5 is THE TRAP: the mac is genuinely golden and was shot under neutral light, so its grey card is ALREADY neutral - the correct move is to HOLD white balance (match exposure only); an agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' move, or 'cools an imagined blue cast', neutralises its card off-neutral and strips the real food colour. Frame 3 carries the bright-red gingham liner for the masked in-family recolor; frame 6's greens must stay true (don't oversaturate). Frame 1 (pastrami) is the featured hero that also branches to the transparent app-hero cutout. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs, index-addressed #01..#08 (no descriptive names) so the agent must open each to decide its treatment.

inputs.name: corner_and_cure_wordmark.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat retro deli wordmark reading 'CORNER & CURE' in a bold condensed vintage signage typeface, chunky cream-white letters with a thin gold keyline, on a solid deep oxblood-maroon field, slight retro press distress. Rendered as if lifted off a printed sign: the ground is a slightly warm off-white paper around the mark (NOT transparent), the whole thing sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg), there is extra paper margin around the mark, and edges are a touch soft. High contrast so that, once cleaned, it vectorizes cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: Slight rotation, off-white paper ground, margin and soft edges are deliberate so image_vectorize fed the raw file would trace the paper and bake in the skew - forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten -> crisp/contrast -> crop-to-bounds -> knock the off-white ground to transparency -> THEN vectorize. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering. IP-clean coined brand mark ('Corner & Cure' is invented, not a real trademark).

inputs.name: brand_direction_note.txt
inputs.gen_prompt: Write a 5-7 line client brand-direction note for Corner & Cure deli: a gritty New-York-deli / Nonna's-kitchen / street-culture aesthetic - warm, characterful and a little chaotic, NOT clean-corporate. State the house look target in plain creative language (warm and golden, deep matte shadows that never go pure black, rich but not neon colour, so every dish reads like the same appetising shoot). State that all dish photos must read as ONE cohesive shoot, that the tiles sit on a rustic counter-paper texture, and that the shop's signature accent colour is a deep oxblood-maroon (so a clashing bright pillar-box red in any shot should be pulled toward that house oxblood, not left shouting). Include the stock-search hint 'crumpled brown butcher paper deli counter texture, warm, gritty, top-down'. Do NOT name any real brand, app, or person.
inputs.realism_notes: The written creative direction; drives the shared house-look target the agent must author from primitives, the Adobe Stock backdrop query, and the in-family oxblood recolor target. States the look as a GOAL in creative language, never as tool settings. Not a pixel asset.

outputs.name: graded_dish_tiles_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized, straightened, tile-cropped deli dish photos pulled to ONE gritty-warm house look, delivered as the tile-framed crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) - the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within +/-3 levels) with the whole set matched to one shared white point while holding the warm-matte house look, and true-to-dish (no dish's genuine colour forced off, the golden mac held); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered tile crop (the *_tile output that binds into that dish's tile) - it is framed on the dish with the grey card fully cropped OUT (no card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is NEVER evaluated on the tile crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move the agent applied to each frame.

outputs.name: CornerAndCure_StorefrontMenu_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready storefront menu tiles - ONE single-record tile per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) - exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each tile binds its dish_name/item_code/price/description/tagline/handle verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralized graded photo dropped into the @Dish frame, the shared graded counter-paper texture into the @Backdrop frame, and the vectorized wordmark into the @Wordmark masthead frame - all by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI at the 4x5in / 1200x1500px tile size. The featured Hand-Cut Pastrami on Rye is simply page one of this merged set, not a separately exported file.

outputs.name: hero_featured_transparent.png
outputs.spec: The featured hero (pastrami-on-rye) lifted onto a transparent background via image_remove_background (outer background only, no reconstruction) so it can drop onto the counter-paper backdrop in the app's large hero slot without a hard rectangular photo edge. Graded to the same house look as the tile set.

outputs.name: hero_app_1080x1350.jpg
outputs.spec: The featured hero graded frame reframed by downscale-crop to EXACTLY 1080x1350 px for the food-delivery app's portrait hero slot - same house look as the tile set, grey card cropped out. Downscale-only from the ~4000-4500 px camera source; never enlarged.

outputs.name: variant_pickle_liner_oxblood.jpg
outputs.spec: Recolored variant of the house-pickles frame: the clashing bright pillar-box red gingham liner deepened to the house oxblood-maroon via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small within-family hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance drop that darkens and mutes the red - an in-band adjacent shift, no near-complementary rotation) riding the liner's existing luminosity, so the gingham weave, its folds and cast shadow stay natural, the white checks stay white, and the pickles/basket/counter are untouched - no whole-image overlay, no flat fill.

outputs.name: corner_and_cure_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the wordmark, traced only after the raw file is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency - razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground or skew.

connector_workflow.note: Search Adobe Stock for a crumpled brown butcher-paper / deli-counter texture using the client's direction-note hint (low-res candidate previews + asset IDs). This is the stock-sourcing beat of the hero brief.
License the chosen counter-paper texture BEFORE use and download it full-res (~4000 px) - becomes the shared tile background.

Grade the licensed backdrop to the SAME warm-matte house white point as the dish set (warm temperature hold, lifted matte blacks that never hit pure black, gentle contrast) so the texture sits under every tile cohesively rather than clashing with the graded food. Built from primitives, not a preset. Report the move.

Featured hero. Triage: this frame is tilted ~4 deg, so level it first (only the tilted frames 1/2/3/8 get straightened; deciding which is part of the job). image_auto_straighten is the ONLY tool that rectifies tilt.

Cool bluish fluorescent cast on a DARK steel counter: WARM it (positive temperature) and set tint until the in-frame grey card reads neutral by eye, then land the house look - lift the crushed shadows carefully so the low-key counter keeps texture without muddying, hold the warm-matte tone and a touch of clarity so the stacked meat reads appetising. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card; do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces the deprecated _color_temperature/_dark_portions and the banned auto_tone/preset shortcuts).

Establish the house colour SIGNATURE the rest of the set is graded toward: a moderate in-family push warming the cured-meat reds/ambers and restraining any stray green, well under ~90 deg (no near-complementary rotation). This is the agent-AUTHORED look built from primitives - not a preset, not auto-tone. The same reasoned target is carried to the other seven frames.

Crop the neutralized+graded hero to the 1200x1500 tile frame, framing on the sandwich with the grey card cropped OUT - this tile crop binds into the featured tile. The pre-crop master (hero_neutralized, card still in frame) is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifact; neutrality is graded THERE, card-exclusion is the separate check here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand.
Second reframe of the same graded hero to EXACTLY 1080x1350 for the app's portrait hero slot (grey card out). Downscale-crop from the ~4000-4500 px camera source - never enlarged past source pixels.

Lift the featured pastrami onto a TRANSPARENT background (outer background only, no reconstruction) so it drops onto the counter-paper backdrop in the app hero slot without a hard rectangular photo edge - the move that kills the collage look. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill).
Tilted ~3 deg under warm tungsten - level it.

Warm tungsten cast on LIGHT butcher paper (high-key): move the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames - COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and it matches the shared white point, and protect the overexposed side by pulling highlights so the light paper doesn't clip. Adaptive: a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here. Land the same warm-matte house look. Report the move.
Crop to the 1200x1500 tile frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~4 deg, cool grey daylight - level it.

Cool daylight cast: warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point and land the house look; keep the pickle green and the brine sheen true. Report the move. This graded full-res frame feeds BOTH the tile crop AND the liner-recolor branch, so keep it before cropping.
Crop to the 1200x1500 tile frame (the standard red-liner version bound into the House Dill Pickles tile), grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

On the graded full-res frame, semantically select ONLY the red gingham deli liner ('the red-and-white checked gingham deli liner'). A real named object, not a hue/coordinate/region selection - isolates the recolor so the pickles, basket and counter are untouched. Returns a maskURI.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes frame + liner mask): keep the liner in the red family but deepen it toward the house oxblood - a small within-band hue nudge (well under ~60 deg, staying in red/wine; NOT a near-complementary rotation) plus a luminance drop that darkens the red, letting the gingham's existing luminosity carry the weave, folds and cast shadow. Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the whole plate) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (kills the weave and the white checks) - both are wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): trim the red-band saturation and settle the luminance so the liner lands on the deep oxblood-maroon house target instead of a flat brick or a still-bright candy red, still riding the original luminosity so the weave and shadow stay natural and the white checks stay white. A deepen-and-mute in the same hue family, not a swing to a new hue.
Resize the finished oxblood liner variant to the tile frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Dim, underexposed, muddy WARM light on a dark diner counter: the dominant move is TONAL - lift exposure and add contrast/clarity to recover the muddy frame - THEN cool slightly to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point. Different problem from the cool-cast frames; a blanket WB-only pass leaves it muddy. Land the house look. Report the move.
Crop to the 1200x1500 tile frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

THE TRAP FRAME. The baked four-cheese mac is genuinely deep golden-brown and was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (match exposure/brightness to the set only, land the matte-shadow house tone). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on frames 1/3/6, or 'cools an imagined blue cast', neutralises the card OFF-neutral and strips the mac's real golden colour - the dish the client is selling. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
Crop to the 1200x1500 tile frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Cool cast on light butcher paper: warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point and land the house look, but keep the romaine/herb greens TRUE - don't oversaturate or let the warm push shove the greens yellow. Report the move.
Crop to the 1200x1500 tile frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Overexposed and warm with clipped highlights on one edge: PULL exposure/highlights down to recover the blown edge FIRST, then cool to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point. Opposite tonal AND WB direction from the underexposed coffee frame - proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Land the house look. Report the move.
Crop to the 1200x1500 tile frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~3 deg - level it.

Near-neutral light: its grey card is close to neutral, so only a SMALL WB nudge is needed to land on the shared white point - over-correcting would push it off the set. Set exposure to match set brightness, land the matte-shadow house tone. Report the (small) move. Frames 1-8 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.
Crop to the 1200x1500 tile frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the mark sits ~2 deg rotated on its paper ground - straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed file to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the off-white paper ground toward white so the cream lettering and gold keyline separate hard from the ground - a soft low-contrast raster traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the paper margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the surrounding field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The mark reads on the tile's oxblood masthead, so a clean transparent knockout is required here.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead. Tracing the raw file instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette - the trap this prep chain avoids.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: pastrami_tile, sub_tile, pickles_tile, coffee_tile, mac_tile, salad_tile, fries_tile, hash_tile, corner_and_cure_wordmark.svg, backdrop_graded
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the eight grey-card-neutralized tile crops plus the vector wordmark and the graded backdrop so the merge can resolve them by the @Dish (per-row photo), @Wordmark (shared mark) and @Backdrop (shared texture) columns. Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @Dish/@Wordmark/@Backdrop columns resolve to for each single-record tile's three image frames.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (dish_name/item_code/price/description/tagline/handle) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve ALL THREE image columns per row - that row's graded photo into the @Dish frame, the shared graded backdrop into the @Backdrop frame, and the vectorized wordmark into the @Wordmark masthead frame - producing EXACTLY ONE merged tile per row (eight tiles). This InDesign layout merge is what binds the images: document_merge_data_vector is TEXT-ONLY and was the original defect. [T] requires the hand-authored template with its three merge-wired image frames; a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind and a multi-record grid is impossible here.

Export the merged single-record tiles to a press-ready ~300 DPI PDF at the 1200x1500 tile size, one tile per dish. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all eight tiles, one page per dish) in a single call - it cannot export one named record on its own, so the featured pastrami is simply page one, not a separate file. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout; the storefront set emerges only from the assembled chain. The backdrop chains asset_search(1) -> asset_license_and_download_stock(2) -> image_apply_adjustments grade(3). Eight per-dish grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame grey card (adaptive per frame: warm the cool-cast frames 1/3/6, cool the warm-cast frames 2/4/7, HOLD white balance on the genuinely-golden mac 5, small nudge on the near-neutral hash 8, lift the underexposed coffee 4, recover the overexposed fries 7), with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 1/2/3/8 and an image_crop_and_resize tile crop after each, so all eight converge on one shared white point and the authored warm-matte house look. The featured hero (frame 1) establishes the house colour signature via image_adjust_hsl(6) and branches three ways from hero_look: the tile crop(7), the exact 1080x1350 app-hero crop(8), and the image_remove_background transparent cutout(9). The pickles frame's neutralized full-res master feeds BOTH its tile crop(15) AND the recolor branch: image_select_by_prompt(16) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(17) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(18) -> resize(19), the two HSL passes both consuming the liner_mask. The wordmark runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain: straighten(31) -> crisp adjustments(32) -> crop_to_bounds(33) -> remove_background to transparency(34) -> vectorize(35). The eight graded tile crops, the wordmark SVG and the graded backdrop converge into the upload session(36) -> finalize(37) -> document_merge_data_layout(38), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the menu roster CSV and emits one merged tile per row, resolving @Dish (that row's graded photo), @Wordmark (the shared vector mark) and @Backdrop (the shared graded texture) into the template's three merge-wired image frames.
